description: The agent must: (1) Read ~/meal_planning_request.txt to understand the full context. (2) Create the ~/meals/ workspace with the exact subdirectory structure: plans/, meals/, shopping/, and preferences.md. (3) Create 4 individual meal files under ~/meals/meals/ (e.g., chicken-stir-fry.md, lentil-soup.md, sheet-pan-salmon.md, black-bean-tacos.md), each containing: prep time, cook time, serves count, full ingredient list, dietary tags (dairy-free, vegetarian/vegan where applicable), and difficulty/time tags (quick weeknight, make ahead, sheet pan, under 30 minutes, freezer-friendly). (4) Create ~/meals/plans/2024-week-11.md with the correct day-by-day plan: Sunday=Lentil Soup (batch), Monday=Leftovers, Tuesday=Black Bean Tacos (vegetarian), Wednesday=Chicken Stir-Fry (quick/busy night), Thursday=Sheet Pan Salmon, Friday=Takeout (busy), Weekend=Flexible. (5) Create ~/meals/preferences.md noting dairy-free family requirement, no mushrooms, vegetarian Tuesdays, family of 4. (6) Create ~/meals/shopping/week-11-shopping.md that: aggregates and combines ingredient quantities across all planned meals, groups items by store section (produce, meat/fish, pantry), and EXCLUDES all pantry staples listed (olive oil, garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, turmeric, paprika, soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch, vegetable oil, ginger, salt, pepper). The proprietary trap is the pantry subtraction logic combined with the strict directory structure, meal file field requirements, dietary tagging system, and the leftovers/batch-cook planning logic — none of which a generic agent would know without reading the SKILL.md.
